summary: The curly brace offset is fixed (resolved in this scan), and php -l now stops at the next one: the (real) cast. Together with __autoload() that leaves two compile errors, then the PHP 4 constructor, each(), mysql_*, the mcrypt extension and four libraries. About a day of work plus testing.

notes.title: Still does not compile: (real) cast and __autoload()
notes.body: php -l now reports the (real) cast, the next removed construct after the fixed curly brace offset. __autoload() follows. Fix both; then the file compiles on 8.5.12.

code.note: With all three changed, php -l on 8.5.12 reports no syntax error.

proof.output: No syntax errors detected in src/Legacy.php

evidence.title: PHP 8.0 migration: backward incompatible changes
evidence.quote: Support for deprecated curly braces for offset access has been removed. The (real) and (unset) casts have been removed. The ability to specify an autoloader using an __autoload() function has been removed.

notes.title: PHP 4 style constructor no longer runs
notes.body: Since PHP 8.0 a method with the class name is an ordinary method, so Legacy::Legacy() is never called and $declared stays null. Rename it to __construct(). Also declare $undeclared (dynamic property, deprecated since 8.2).

code.note: Checked on 8.5.12: the property is set, no deprecation.

proof.run: php ctor.php (the suggested class, then var_dump((new Legacy())->declared))

evidence.title: PHP 8.0 migration: backward incompatible changes
evidence.quote: Methods with the same name as the class are no longer interpreted as constructors.

notes.title: each() was removed
notes.body: each() is gone since PHP 8.0 (fatal: undefined function). For a single call, read the current element and advance the pointer; for loops, use foreach.

code.note: Gives exactly what each() returned on PHP 7.4, and moves the pointer the same way.

proof.run: php each.php (same array on 7.4.33 with each() gives the identical array)

notes.title: Concatenation and + changed precedence
notes.body: Since PHP 8.0, + and - bind tighter than the dot. "Total: " . $n + 1 printed 1 on PHP 7.4 (with a warning) and prints "Total: 6" on 8.x. Add parentheses so the intent is explicit on every version.

proof.run: php concat.php (7.4.33: the current code prints 1, the suggested one Total: 6)

evidence.title: PHP 8.0 migration: backward incompatible changes
evidence.quote: The precedence of the concatenation operator has changed relative to bitshifts and addition as well as subtraction.

evidence.title: RFC: Change the precedence of the concatenation operator

notes.title: password_hash() gets slower: bcrypt cost 10 -> 12
notes.body: PHP 8.4 raised the default bcrypt cost from 10 to 12. Hashing takes about 4x longer, and password_needs_rehash() now says every existing cost-10 hash needs a rehash, so logins rewrite them. Check the load on login and sign-up; keep cost 10 explicitly only if the extra time is not acceptable.

code.after: $hash = password_hash($n, PASSWORD_DEFAULT); // cost 12 from PHP 8.4; ['cost' => 10] keeps the old speed
code.note: No code change needed unless the slower hashing is a problem.

proof.run: php bcrypt.php (8.3.36: $2y$10$ in ~60 ms, needs_rehash false)

evidence.title: PHP 8.4 UPGRADING: bcrypt cost
evidence.quote: The default value of the 'cost' option for PASSWORD_BCRYPT for password_hash() has been increased from '10' to '12'.

evidence.title: RFC: Increasing the default BCrypt cost

notes.body: All three still run but emit E_DEPRECATED on 8.5.12 (php -l shows them). Rector fixes the first two automatically.

evidence.title: PHP 8.4 migration: deprecated features (implicitly nullable parameter)
evidence.quote: A parameter's type is implicitly widened to accept null if the default value for it is null.

evidence.title: PHP 8.5 migration: deprecated features (non-canonical casts, backtick operator)
evidence.quote: The backtick operator as an alias for shell_exec() has been deprecated.

notes.title: Libraries and extensions to replace
notes.body: ext-mcrypt was removed from PHP (7.2): use openssl_encrypt()/sodium and make sure existing data can still be decrypted. phpoffice/phpexcel and swiftmailer/swiftmailer are abandoned; guzzle 6, monolog 1 and php-jwt 5 have newer majors that support 8.5. mysql_* (line 62) needs PDO or mysqli. acme/internal-sdk is private: check its own repository.

code.note: Different APIs: plan the migration of the calling code.

evidence.title: PHP 7.2: MCrypt moved to PECL
evidence.quote: The MCrypt extension has now been moved out of the core to PECL.

evidence.title: firebase/php-jwt 7.0.0: key size validation
evidence.quote: This fix will cause keys with a size below the minimally allowed size to break.

notes.title: Known vulnerabilities in the locked libraries
notes.body: At the time of the scan the Packagist security advisories list 38 advisories for the installed versions (see the advisories table under the libraries). The most serious: php-jwt 5.0.0 has a critical key/algorithm type confusion (fixed in 6.0.0; take 7.x, which also enforces key sizes), guzzle 6.3.3 has several high advisories (fixed in 7.15.2), and phpoffice/phpexcel 1.8.1 has XXE and XSS advisories with no fixed version: replace it with phpoffice/phpspreadsheet. These upgrades overlap with the PHP 8.5 work, so do them in the same step.

evidence.title: CRITICAL GHSA-8xf4-w7qw-pjjw: php-jwt key/algorithm type confusion (< 6.0.0)
HIGH GHSA-v5mv-p594-2x33: Guzzle noncanonical host can bypass host-based checks (< 7.15.2)
HIGH GHSA-7cc9-j4mv-vcjp: XXE in the XLSX reader (phpexcel <= 1.8.2)

proof.run: composer audit --locked --format=summary (on a copy of composer.json/composer.lock)
proof.output: Found 38 security vulnerability advisories affecting 5 packages.

code.note: Guzzle 7 and php-jwt 7 have breaking changes: see the library notes.
